projects.name: Vision-SL
projects.category: Computer Vision / Accessibility / Sign Language Learning
projects.description: Exploring accessible sign language learning through computer vision and offline-first desktop applications.

people.name: Felicia Chuma
people.urlNote: Ask Felicia which link, if any, she wants credited.

projects.approach: Vision-SL has three Linux desktop applications: Admin, Teacher and Student. The Admin application creates a LAN server. Teacher and Student applications discover the server on the local network. Teachers can add signs, create assignments and view coursework. Assignments are automatically marked. Students receive assignments and practise signs. MediaPipe is used for hand tracking. Sign-related data is administered through the Admin application.

apps.name: Admin
apps.role: Creates the LAN server; administers sign-related data

diagram.title: Vision-SL: three desktop apps on one local network
diagram.description: The Admin application creates a LAN server and holds sign data. Teacher and Student applications discover that server on the local network. Teachers add signs and set assignments; students practise signs with MediaPipe hand tracking, and assignments are marked automatically.
